data.name: Saket
data.gender_notes: Saket is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Saket is derived from the Sanskrit word 'saketas' which means 'belonging to the forest deity'. In Hindu mythology, Saket is the name of a divine forest where Lord Rama spent some time during his exile. It is a popular name among Hindus, especially in India, and is often given to boys. The name Saket carries the meaning “Forest Deity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Saket usually hope their child will grow to embody forest deity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Connection to nature and divine protection.
data.etymology: Saket belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Forest Deity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Saket total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Saket carries a rich cultural heritage and holds significant importance in Indian history. Being derived from the term 'saketas' which means 'belonging to the forest deity', it has roots in the ancient Hindu tales and mythology. The name also brings to mind the story of Lord Rama and his time spent in exile in the enchanted forest of Saket. It is a name that evokes purity, spiritual growth, and connection to nature.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Saket holds deep spiritual resonance as it is associated with the divine forest where Lord Rama found inner peace and strength during his exile. The name symbolizes the connection between the divine and the natural world and serves as a reminder to seek inner peace and serenity, no matter the circumstances in life. It is a name that inspires one to cultivate inner calmness and find solace in nature, just as Lord Rama did in the forest of Saket.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Saket, meaning 'forest of Shiva', symbolizes the deep connection and immersion in the divine wisdom and peace that one finds in the natural world and within oneself. It is a reminder to seek enlightenment through the tranquility of nature and the inner self.

vedic_reference.note: Saket is a name of the sage Vashistha and also a place name, such as the ancient city of Saket, near present-day Delhi.

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata mentions a forest named Saketaka, which was part of the extensive forest of Kamyaka. It was the site of a great battle during the Mahabharata war between the Pandavas and the Kauravas.

Another reference to Saket is in connection with the ancient Indian city of Saketa (modern day Sankasya), which was a major Buddhist pilgrimage site. The city was considered as one of the eight Mahasanghas (great assemblies) of ancient India and was known for its concentration of Buddhist monasteries and scholarly discourse.
